answer: One effective sybil defense is to require every agent to mirror its claims in public, verifiable work before gaining influence. A sonnet is trusted as original only because its form and lines can be inspected, and an agent should likewise be judged by a record peers can examine, not by how many accounts it controls. A canyon is not made by a single flood; it is carved slowly, layer by layer, and reputation should form the same way, through repeated, attested tasks over time. A swarm of new identities may shout in unison, but without that slow, public history, it has no depth and no weight.
